issues.body:
`_private_probe_rows()` (metrics-alert.py:148-149) uses `(0, '{"private": []}')` as its fifth fixture, and the row is named "visibility probe: non-boolean private" with want=False.

Mutate the gate at metrics-alert.py:122 from `payload.get("private") is True` to `bool(payload.get("private"))` (or `== True`) and walk all five rows: `true`->True ok; `false`->False ok; rc=9->False ok; `not-json`->False ok; `[]` -> `bool([])` is False -> **still False, row still green**. All six metrics rows survive the mutant. The row that exists to pin strictness pins nothing beyond what the `{"private": false}` row already pins.

That mutant is the fail-OPEN direction of this PR's own gate: under it, a GitHub payload carrying `"private": "false"` (string) or `1` would confirm the destination as private and route the alert to an unverified ALERT_REPO under ALERT_TOKEN.

The other five copies do kill it, precisely because their fixtures are truthy: ci-latency `"true"` (line 955), groom-mint `"true"`, dispatch-stall `1`, triage `1`, park-stock `"yes"`. So does the audited reference, groom-alert.py:396 (`{"private": "true"}`). metrics is the sole deviation, in the file whose whole premise is that the six copies are identical — and it deviates in exactly the direction that removes the assertion.

Per the repo's own rule (a self-test that would pass regardless of the code is a blocker), a named row that does not flip red on the wrongness it names is not a valid test.
issues.fix_hint: In scripts/metrics-alert.py:149 change the fifth fixture from `(0, '{"private": []}')` to a TRUTHY non-boolean, matching the audited reference: `(0, '{"private": "true"}')` (groom-alert.py:396) or `(0, '{"private": 1}')` (dispatch-stall/triage). Verify by mutation: temporarily replace `is True` with a truthy test at metrics-alert.py:122 and confirm `visibility probe: non-boolean private` goes FAIL before restoring.
issues.title: Vacuous strictness row: metrics' "non-boolean private" fixture `{"private": []}` is FALSY, so it cannot kill the `is True` -> truthy weakening

issues.body:
ci-latency-alert.py:928, dispatch-stall-alert.py:169, groom-mint-alert.py:171 and metrics-alert.py:126 all now state the router has "identical semantics and signature to the other alert routers: ALERT_REPO is selected ONLY when its token is present, it differs from the registry case-insensitively, and a live GET /repos/{ALERT_REPO} under that token confirms a literal `private: true`."

Enumerating every router in the tree: ten now carry the 4-arg confirmed-private form (the six here plus groom/usage/plan-alert), but TWO do not — `scripts/ratelimit-alert.py:363` and `scripts/ledger-identity-watch.py:245` both keep `def _alert_route(alert_repo, alert_token, registry_repo)` with the bare `if alert_repo and alert_token: return alert_repo, alert_token`.

This is not theoretical. `.github/workflows/groom-sweep.yml:696` runs `ratelimit-alert.py` on the scheduled sweep with `ALERT_REPO`/`ALERT_TOKEN` mounted at lines 692-693. So after this PR the exact defect #1775 exists to close is still live on a cron lane, while the governed prose in four other files asserts the estate is uniform.

The inconsistency also runs the other way: ratelimit-alert.py:364-366 says it is "identical semantics to groom-alert/ci-latency-alert/park-stock-alert: the private ALERT_REPO only when ALERT_TOKEN can write there" — naming three routers this PR changes, and asserting of them a claim that is now false (and using "can write there", one of the 16 governed `phrasings`). groom-sweep.yml:833 carries the same stale sentence.

In a repo where the router docstring is pinned by EQUALITY and treated as the contract, a pinned sentence that overstates coverage is the failure mode the guard exists to prevent: a reader auditing the trust surface concludes the fail-open is closed everywhere when two live routers still have it. The behavioural gap in ratelimit-alert.py is pre-existing; the FALSE claim about it is introduced by this diff.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) extend the change to scripts/ratelimit-alert.py and scripts/ledger-identity-watch.py so the claim becomes true — same `_repo_confirmed_private` + 4-arg `_alert_route` + `_private_probe_rows` rows, and refresh ratelimit-alert.py:364-366 and .github/workflows/groom-sweep.yml:833 — or (b) narrow the prose in ci-latency-alert.py:928, dispatch-stall-alert.py:169, groom-mint-alert.py:171 and metrics-alert.py:126 to name the routers it is actually identical to (e.g. "identical semantics and signature to the groom/usage/plan/park-stock/triage/metrics/dispatch-stall/ci-latency/groom-mint copies; scripts/ratelimit-alert.py and scripts/ledger-identity-watch.py have NOT yet been migrated — issue #NNNN"), and file the follow-up. (b) is a prose-only fix; (a) is the one that closes the live cron lane.
issues.title: The new docstrings claim identity with "the other alert routers", but ratelimit-alert.py (live on cron with ALERT_REPO/ALERT_TOKEN) and ledger-identity-watch.py still route on PRESENCE alone

issues.body:
Independently re-verified this round. Every `_alert_route` call in these three self-tests either injects a lambda or short-circuits before the default is read:

- ci-latency-alert.py: lines 1843/1845/1849 inject lambdas; 1852 (`token=None`) and 1854 (`repo=None`) fail the `if alert_repo and alert_token` guard. The only other call site is `main()` at line 2553, and no flow harness in this file sets `ALERT_REPO`.
- dispatch-stall-alert.py: 755/758/762 inject lambdas; 766/767 short-circuit; the flow harness at line 1119 explicitly `os.environ.pop("ALERT_REPO", None)`.
- triage-stock-alert.py: 729 injects a lambda; 731/732 short-circuit; 1030/1034/1038 inject lambdas; 1043/1046 short-circuit. No harness sets ALERT_REPO.

So mutating line 935 (and its siblings) to `else (lambda r, t: True)` — the exact fail-open this PR exists to close — leaves those three files fully green: the probe rows call `_repo_confirmed_private` directly and never consult the default, and the route rows never evaluate the default expression at all. In those three files even a misspelled callee would only surface in production.

Still minor, not blocking: the helper's own fail-closed branches are fully pinned, the binding is textually identical to the audited groom-alert.py reference, and groom-mint (line 1358 stub), metrics (line 802 `responses[("api", "repos/org/private")]`) and park-stock (line 712 fake_run) do drive it end-to-end via `main()`.
issues.fix_hint: Cheapest kill for the three uncovered files: inside the `_private_probe_rows` window (while `_gh` is still swapped) call the router with NO injected lambda and assert both directions — `_alert_route("org/private", "tok", "org/registry") == ("org/private", "tok")` on the `private: true` stub and `== ("org/registry", None)` on the `private: false` stub. That pins the default binding without needing a full `main()` harness. groom-alert.py:356-362 is the end-to-end reference form.
issues.title: The `confirmed_private=None -> _repo_confirmed_private` default binding is still never evaluated in ci-latency, dispatch-stall or triage (round-2 carryover, re-verified)

issues.body:
Every `_private_probe_rows()` fixture set feeds a JSON object or a parse failure. None feeds valid JSON whose top level is not a dict — e.g. `"null"` (`json.loads` -> None) or `"[]"` (-> list). Both are shapes `gh api` can emit on an odd response.

Consequence: delete `isinstance(payload, dict) and` from `_repo_confirmed_private` (dispatch-stall-alert.py:162, and the same line in the other five) and all thirty-six probe rows stay green — but in production a `null` body would raise `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'` INSIDE `_alert_route`, which is called unguarded from `main()` (dispatch-stall-alert.py:591, ci-latency-alert.py:2553, groom-mint-alert.py:584, triage-stock-alert.py:475). The alert run aborts and the alert is never posted — the single outcome every one of these docstrings promises can never happen ("never silently losing the alert").

The audited reference (groom-alert.py:383-398) has the same gap, so this is a consistent hole rather than a deviation — flagging it because this PR is the change that introduces the guard, and a guard with no killing row is the shape this repo blocks on.
issues.fix_hint: Add a sixth fixture to each `_private_probe_rows()` tuple — `(0, "null")` (and optionally `(0, "[]")`) — extend the `want` tuple with `False`, and name the row "visibility probe: non-object payload". Confirm it is killing by temporarily removing `isinstance(payload, dict) and`: the row must ERROR/FAIL, not pass.
issues.title: The `isinstance(payload, dict)` guard is unexercised in all six copies; dropping it turns a `null`/list body into an AttributeError that LOSES the alert

issues.body:
`_repo_confirmed_private` calls `_gh(..., capture=True, token=token)` with `check=False`, so a transient rc!=0 (rate limit, 5xx, expired ALERT_TOKEN, network) prints nothing. `_alert_route` then returns `(registry_repo, None)` and `main()` (triage-stock-alert.py:475, and the equivalents in the other five) posts the alert to the public registry without logging the routing decision or the reason for the downgrade.

The availability posture is right — the alert still lands, never lost. The confidentiality posture is a new path: before this PR a correctly-configured private ALERT_REPO always received the alert; now a single failed lookup publishes that same body publicly, indefinitely and silently, and an operator who set ALERT_REPO has no way to learn their alerts stopped going there.

The mitigation is real and I checked it: each docstring now enumerates what the body contains ("public issue-routing state", "public workflow names, run links, and latency measurements", etc.), and park-stock/triage pin that sentence by equality. So this is a documented trade-off, not a defect — but the trade-off is undetectable in operation. Contrast `_gh_json`, which does emit `::warning::` on both failure shapes.
issues.fix_hint: Pass `check=True` to the `_gh` call in `_repo_confirmed_private` (it already prints only `args[0]`/`args[1]` and a returncode — never stderr, never the token), or emit an explicit `::warning::<script>: ALERT_REPO visibility unconfirmed (rc=...), routing this alert to the registry` from the `not confirmed` branch of `_alert_route`. Pin it with a row asserting the message is emitted on rc!=0 and NOT emitted on the confirmed-private path.
issues.title: A failed visibility probe silently reroutes a private-destined alert to the PUBLIC registry with no operator signal

issues.body:
dispatch-stall, groom-mint, metrics, park-stock and triage all carry the semicolon-joined form (`calls.append((args, kwargs)); return type(...)()`, `_gh = response(rc, body); values.append(...)`, `finally: _gh = original`), no blank line before the nested `def response`, several lines past the ~100-column width the surrounding modules hold, and no docstring.

ci-latency-alert.py:941-960 has the SAME helper written out properly, with the docstring "Exercise every fail-closed result of this module's live repository probe". Since the stated intent of these copies is to be identical, the five compressed ones are the odd ones out.

No lint config or lint job exists in this repo, so this does not break CI — it is readability only, in files whose value proposition is that a reviewer can read the authority surface at a glance. Unchanged since round 2.
issues.fix_hint: Reformat the five compressed copies to match scripts/ci-latency-alert.py:941-960 verbatim (blank line before the nested `def`, one statement per line, `finally:` on its own line, the same one-line docstring), so the six copies really are identical and a future diff to one is visibly a diff to all.
issues.title: `_private_probe_rows` is written in a compressed style in five of six files, inconsistent with the sixth (round-2 carryover, unchanged)

issues.body:
`ambient()` (park-stock-alert.py:730-734) was `routed("api")[1]`; it now scans for the `/pulls?` call and returns `None` if none is found. The half-configured rows assert `routed("issue", "create") == (REGISTRY, ambient())`.

If the census read ever stopped being issued, `ambient()` returns `None`, and `routed("issue", "create")[1]` is also `None` whenever GH_TOKEN is unset in the harness environment (the registry fallback passes `token=None`, so `_gh` never sets it) — the row would then pass on two absences rather than on a match.

Well contained in practice: `main()` cannot reach `upsert` without `read_pulls`, and the row at lines 764-769 explicitly pins `api_cmd is not None`. The `/pulls?` disambiguation itself is correct and necessary — without it the new `repos/{repo}` probe would be mistaken for the PR census read. Flagged only because the sibling `routed()` helper documents exactly this hazard and `ambient()` no longer holds that property. Unchanged since round 2.
issues.fix_hint: Give `ambient()` the same fail-loud shape as `routed()`: return a distinct sentinel (or raise) when no `/pulls?` call was recorded, so a vanished census read reds the two fallback rows instead of satisfying them by mutual absence.
issues.title: `ambient()` now returns None when the census read is absent, so the two fallback rows can pass by comparing two absences (round-2 carryover, unchanged)

verdict.summary:
The head is UNCHANGED since round 2 (still 107a42168), so this diff is byte-identical to the one round 2 approved. The two blocking findings are review-side discoveries, not a code regression — but per the stated scale (new findings at higher severity) progress is "regressing".

What is right: `_repo_confirmed_private` is a correct fail-closed probe (rc!=0, unparseable, non-dict, `private is not True` -> False); `_alert_route` narrows strictly, so every new path is a tightening; the token goes via `_gh(token=)` into env, never argv. `_private_probe_rows` restores `_gh` in a `finally`, and `probe_call` pins the GET-only shape and route-token threading. park-stock/triage governed prose holds: the new anchor occurs exactly once, the wording trips none of the 16 `phrasings`, and the census reports `[]` over a scan proven to cover the router. metrics' AST `api_shapes` row is real — exactly one `_gh(["api",...])` call site exists, so an added api call, a non-f-string path or any `-X/--method/-f/--input` reds it.

Blocking (1): metrics' "non-boolean private" fixture is `{"private": []}` — FALSY. Weakening `is True` to a truthy test leaves every metrics row green. The audited reference (groom-alert.py:396) uses `{"private": "true"}`; the other five copies use truthy values. metrics is the one copy whose strictness row pins no strictness.

Blocking (2): four docstrings now claim identity with "the other alert routers" while scripts/ratelimit-alert.py:363 and scripts/ledger-identity-watch.py:245 keep the 3-arg presence-only form — and ratelimit-alert.py runs on cron at groom-sweep.yml:696 under ALERT_REPO/ALERT_TOKEN (692-693). The prose asserts a uniformity the estate lacks, over a live fail-open.

Bash was denied, so `--self-test` was not executed; findings are from reading the head tree. Tree byte-identical apart from this file.
